parameters.query:
=What significant developments happened in the {{ $json.industry }} industry (MCC Code {{ $json.code }})
in the last 30 days that would matter to a payment-processing risk team?

Cover, with specific names, dates, and sources:

1. Federal or state government actions — regulatory rulings, agency
   enforcement, new legislation, proposed rules. Specify the agency
   (DOT, FAA, FTC, CFPB, SEC, FDA, DEA, etc.).

2. Industry health — bankruptcies, Chapter 11 filings, major company
   distress, consolidation, mass layoffs of meaningful players.

3. Demand-side trends — consumer behavior shifts, declining usage,
   pricing pressure, macro factors affecting this industry.

4. Card-brand actions or chargeback monitoring program changes
   (Visa VDMP, Mastercard ECP) for this MCC.

5. Material litigation against the industry or key players.

Be specific and source everything. If there's no news in a category,
say so explicitly.

parameters.text:
=You are a senior risk analyst at Sentinel Payments evaluating the {{ $('Merge: Merchants + MCC Codes').item.json.industry }} industry (MCC {{ $('Merge: Merchants + MCC Codes').item.json.code }}) for this month's risk review.

Visa's baseline risk rating for this MCC: {{ $('Merge: Merchants + MCC Codes').item.json.mcc_risk_score }} out of 5.

Recent industry research:
{{ $json.results.map(r => '[' + r.date + '] ' + r.title + '\nSource: ' + r.url + '\n' + r.snippet).join('\n\n---\n\n') }}

Your task: assess the current risk for this industry based on the research above. Consider both the baseline MCC risk AND the direction the industry is moving right now.

Produce:
- rating: 1 (very low) to 5 (very high)
- direction: improving, stable, or deteriorating
- summary: a TWO-SENTENCE summary, maximum 400 characters total, of what is moving and why Sentinel should care
- key_flags: exactly 3 flags, each with category (govt_action, industry_health, demand, card_brand, litigation), a one-line headline (maximum 110 characters - this is rendered as a single bullet on a slide), and a source
- rec_action: monitor, document_request, reserve_review, or escalate

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
SLIDE OUTPUT CONSTRAINTS (HARD LIMITS - the Risk Committee deck has fixed slide real estate)
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
- summary: ≤ 400 characters, ending with a period. Two short sentences.
- key_flags[].headline: ≤ 110 characters, one line, no trailing ellipsis.
- Exactly 3 key flags - no more, no fewer.

Be specific. Tie findings to the research provided. Do not invent details. Write tight - every word must earn its place.

parameters.text:
=You are a senior risk analyst at Sentinel Payments — a mid-market US payment processor — evaluating a merchant in our portfolio for the monthly risk review. Your job is to recommend ONE action for this merchant, grounded in Sentinel policy and our history of prior Risk Committee decisions. You recommend; the Risk Committee decides.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
MERCHANT UNDER REVIEW
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Merchant: {{ $json.name }} (ID {{ $json.merchant_id }})
Owner: {{ $json.owner_name }}
MCC: {{ $json.mcc }}
Current month metrics:
  - Chargeback rate: {{ $json.metrics.cb_rate }}
  - Refund rate: {{ $json.metrics.refund_rate }}
  - Internal risk score: {{ $json.metrics.exposure_score }} / 5

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
EVIDENCE GATHERED THIS MONTH (from external sources)
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

OFAC / PEP screening (OpenSanctions):
{{ JSON.stringify($json.ofac_pep_hits) }}

Website content classification (Firecrawl + Claude):
  - Primary vertical: {{ $json.site_classification.primary_vertical }}
  - Restricted verticals found: {{ JSON.stringify($json.site_classification.restricted_verticals_found) }}
  - Red flags: {{ JSON.stringify($json.site_classification.red_flags) }}
  - Notes: {{ $json.site_classification.notes }}

Litigation searches (CourtListener):
  - By company name: {{ $json.litigation_company.count }} cases — {{ JSON.stringify($json.litigation_company.cases) }}
  - By owner name: {{ $json.litigation_owner.count }} cases — {{ JSON.stringify($json.litigation_owner.cases) }}

Public reviews (Google via Apify):
  - Rating: {{ $json.google_reviews.rating }} ({{ $json.google_reviews.review_count }} reviews)
  - Negative review sample: {{ JSON.stringify($json.google_reviews.negative_reviews) }}

Adverse media (Tavily — negative news on business + owner):
{{ JSON.stringify($json.adverse_media) }}

Findings summary: {{ $json.findings_summary }}

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
SENTINEL RISK POLICY (these ARE the rules — apply them)
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

▸ RESERVE POLICY BY MCC TIER
  Base rolling reserve by MCC risk tier (1-5):
    Tier 1 (very low):  no reserve required if CB rate < 0.3%
    Tier 2 (low):       3% rolling reserve, 30-day
    Tier 3 (moderate):  6% rolling reserve, 60-day
    Tier 4 (elevated): 10% rolling reserve, 90-day, monthly Risk review
    Tier 5 (high):     15% reserve floor, case-by-case ceiling, quarterly Risk Committee review

▸ CHARGEBACK THRESHOLD PLAYBOOK
  Two consecutive months at these bands trigger action:
    < 0.3%        — no action
    0.3%-0.5%     — informational monitoring; flag for next-month review
    0.5%-0.7%     — formal documentation request via Risk Analyst; reserve review
    0.7%-0.9%     — mandatory reserve increase per MCC tier; consider rolling_hold_30d
    0.9%-1.0%     — Visa VDMP threshold reached; rolling_hold_30d + reserve at MCC tier ceiling; Risk Analyst review
    ≥ 1.0%        — escalate to Risk Committee for offboarding decision

▸ REFUND RATE MONITORING STANDARDS
  Standard bands (two consecutive months):
    < 2%             — normal; no action
    2%-4%            — informational monitoring
    4%-6%            — formal documentation request via Risk Analyst
    6%-8%            — reserve review + service-quality investigation
    8%-12%           — escalate to Risk Analyst for service-quality / fraud investigation
    > 12% sustained  — escalate to Risk Committee for offboarding decision
    > 15% any single month — immediate investigation + processing hold pending Risk Committee review

  Vertical-specific refund modifier:
    For MCC 5968 (Continuity / Subscription Merchants) and MCC 5499 (Misc Food Stores
    — supplements, wellness, specialty), refund-rate thresholds shift up by 3 percentage
    points before triggering action.

▸ RESTRICTED BUSINESS TYPES POLICY (STRICT LIABILITY)
  Sentinel will NOT process for: marijuana (THC), kratom, unlicensed GLP-1 prescribing,
  unlicensed payday lending, FFL-noncompliant firearms, supplements making unsupported
  FDA claims, illegal gambling, non-consent adult content. CBD is permitted ONLY under
  MCC 5912 with proper pharmacy licensing — never under MCC 5462, 5499, 5814, or any
  non-pharmacy MCC.

  CRITICAL: Restricted product found via site classification under a non-matching MCC
  is grounds for IMMEDIATE escalate_offboarding regardless of other metrics.

▸ BENEFICIAL OWNER RE-SCREENING POLICY (§4.2)
  All beneficial owners are re-screened monthly against OFAC SDN, PEP lists, and
  Sentinel's internal offboarded-entity registry. ANY name match against a BO who
  appears in a prior Sentinel offboarding decision triggers MANDATORY escalation.

▸ OFAC / PEP HIT HANDLING
  Positive OFAC SDN match (exact or fuzzy confidence ≥0.85) = immediate processing
  hold + escalate to Sentinel Compliance.

▸ WEBSITE VERTICAL DRIFT POLICY
  Drift into restricted territory = treated as misclassification and grounds for
  escalate_offboarding per Restricted Business Types Policy.

▸ LITIGATION DISCLOSURE POLICY
  Material pending litigation involving fraud, consumer protection violations, or
  breach of fiduciary duty triggers documentation request via Risk Analyst.

▸ ACTION RECOMMENDATION FRAMEWORK
  Recommend exactly ONE action per merchant per cycle:
    no_action            — monitor only
    request_docs         — formal request for updated processing volumes
    raise_reserve        — increase rolling reserve % per MCC tier ceiling
    rolling_hold_30d     — apply 30-day rolling settlement hold
    escalate_offboarding — refer to Risk Committee for offboarding decision

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
PRIOR DECISIONS TOOL (Pinecone)
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Use the Pinecone tool to retrieve Sentinel's prior Risk Committee decisions on
merchants with comparable characteristics.

TOOL CALL DISCIPLINE:
- Make at most TWO Pinecone queries. After two queries, you MUST stop calling
  tools and produce your final JSON answer.
- Do not output tool-call syntax as part of your text response.
- Your final response must be valid JSON matching the schema.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
TASK
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Recommend ONE action. Your rationale MUST cite specific evidence findings,
specific Sentinel policies by name, and specific prior Risk Committee decisions.

Two HARD ESCALATION triggers — these override everything else:
  1. Restricted product found via site classification under a non-matching MCC.
  2. Beneficial owner name appears in a prior Sentinel offboarding decision.

In all other cases, be calibrated — not reflexively conservative.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
SLIDE OUTPUT CONSTRAINTS (HARD LIMITS - the Risk Committee deck has fixed slide real estate)
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

These constraints are NON-NEGOTIABLE. Write tight or your output gets truncated downstream.

- primary_drivers:   EXACTLY 3 items, each ≤ 120 characters. Short bullet phrases. No trailing periods.
- policy_citations:  EXACTLY 3 items, each ≤ 120 characters. Format: 'Policy name - one-line reason invoked'.
- proposed_actions:  EXACTLY 3 items, each ≤ 120 characters. Imperative voice ('Place rolling 30-day hold').
- prior_precedent.case_summary: 2-3 short sentences, ≤ 300 characters TOTAL. Name the prior merchant + outcome.
- prior_precedent.outcome:      Single phrase, ≤ 140 characters.
- rationale:         3-4 sentences, ≤ 500 characters TOTAL. End with a period. Plain English for the Risk Committee deck.

Pick the 3 STRONGEST drivers / policies / actions. Don't pad lists. Don't restate the same point twice. The Risk Committee will read this on a slide — make every word count.

parameters.content:
# Part 2 Main Workflow

In this section of the workflow, we will get the updates on industry MCC codes, updates on the high risk or watch accounts, and get the data from our portfolio. We want to format this data and save it back into the DB
Fake Example Decisions based on merchant risk are stored in here

# Part 1 Simple RAG Ingestion
Each past decision is stored as a chunk in the Vector DB

# Part 3 Cowork Workflow
This workflow will run from cowork, grab the exact data we need, and send the data back to cowork to build the slide deck
Send Data Back to Claude Cowork
Grab Saved We Stored From the Previous Workflow

# Read Me

This template runs a monthly risk review that pulls merchant and MCC data from Supabase, researches industry changes with Perplexity, screens high-risk merchants using OpenSanctions, CourtListener, Apify, Tavily, and Firecrawl, and uses Anthropic Claude plus Pinecone to store risk snapshots and recommendations.

It consists 3 different workflows. Each one should be saved into individual workflows.

The goal of these workflows is to automate a tedious process of creating a monthly merchant and industry review deck a task that might take a risk team 20+ hours to build


1. Runs on a monthly schedule and initializes the run metadata (month, execution ID, timestamp).
2. Retrieves active merchants and MCC reference data from Supabase, groups merchants by MCC, and uses Perplexity plus Claude to generate an MCC risk snapshot with key flags and a recommended action.
3. Writes each MCC snapshot back to Supabase and aggregates all MCC snapshots for the run.
4. Pulls high-risk merchants for the current month from Supabase and gathers external signals by screening names with OpenSanctions, searching recent cases in CourtListener, fetching recent Google reviews via Apify, and collecting adverse media via Tavily.
5. Scrapes each merchant website with Firecrawl and uses Claude to classify the business vertical and flag restricted content.
6. Uses Claude with Pinecone retrieval of prior Risk Committee decisions (embedded with OpenAI) to produce a single recommended action per merchant and inserts those recommendations into Supabase.
7. Calculates 12-month portfolio trends from Supabase metrics, generates a short portfolio narrative with Claude, saves it to Supabase, and records a monthly manifest summarizing the run.
8. Exposes a webhook that fetches the stored Supabase data for a requested month, formats it for downstream slide-building, and returns the JSON response.

# Setup

1. Create and connect credentials for Supabase, Anthropic (Claude), Perplexity, OpenAI (embeddings), Pinecone, Apify, Tavily, Firecrawl, and the two HTTP header auth credentials used for OpenSanctions and CourtListener.
2. In Supabase, create/confirm the required tables and fields referenced by the workflow (merchants, mcc_codes, monthly_metrics, mcc_risk_snapshots, recommended_actions, portfolio_snapshots, monthly_manifest).
3. Populate the Pinecone index name (n8nrisk) and run the manual ingestion workflow to embed and insert the provided prior decision examples before enabling the monthly recommendation step.
4. Update any environment-specific constants such as the webhook path usage in your slide-building tool and verify the Supabase filters match your month format (yyyy-MM) and risk thresholds.
5. If using the webhook integration, copy the production webhook URL and configure it in your external deck builder (for example, Claude “cowork”) to request the month parameter as needed.

results.title: Summer solstice in Mars’ southern hemisphere is April 25 - EarthSky
results.content: # Summer solstice in Mars’ southern hemisphere is April 25. ### Summer solstice in Mars’ southern hemisphere. Like Earth, Mars tilts on its axis with respect to its orbit around the sun. And Mars’ summer solstice for its southern hemisphere arrives on April 25, 2026. ### Like Earth, Mars has 4 seasons. Mars takes 687 Earth-days to orbit the sun once. So each season on Mars – winter, spring, summer, fall – lasts roughly twice as long as a season on Earth. So – now, in April 2026, as Mars’ northern hemisphere of is tipping into the deepest part of winter – its southern hemisphere is celebrating summer. But there’s still seasonal change, just as there is in the most Mars-like places on Earth … Antarctica, for example. Bottom line: The summer solstice on Mars’ southern hemisphere happens on April 25, 2026. Join now to receive free daily science news delivered straight to your email.

results.title: Flexible International Payments: Klarna Pairs with Worldline - FinTech Magazine
results.content: # Flexible International Payments: Klarna Pairs with Worldline. European payments giant Worldline has deepened its integration with global neobank Klarna to scale BNPL across online and in-store checkouts for e-commerce. European payment services leader Worldline and global digital bank Klarna have signed a major framework agreement to expand access to flexible payment options. The partnership will see Worldline integrate Klarna deeply into its technology stack and handle transaction acquiring, simplifying how merchants deploy these payment methods. The initial rollout will focus on the Global Collect platform, Worldline’s online payment solution tailored for international e-commerce merchants operating in the travel and digital sectors. The final stage of the agreement will see Worldline extend Klarna’s payment suite, including its popular BNPL services, to physical in-store point of sale terminals. “Leveraging our strong local presence, this collaboration will introduce BNPL services across markets, delivering real value for merchants and consumers alike, whether for online or in-person transactions while driving growth across Europe.”.

results.title: Supreme Court lets Andrew Cuomo off the hook for 'wrongful death' of COVID nursing home patients - New York Post
results.content: # Supreme Court lets Andrew Cuomo off the hook for ‘wrongful death’ of COVID nursing home patients. WASHINGTON — The Supreme Court on Monday declined to revive a wrongful death lawsuit that had been rejected by the lower courts against former Gov. Andrew Cuomo over his controversial COVID-19 era nursing home policy. In its Monday order list, the high court denied certiorari, or appeal, of the lower court’s rulings in the lawsuit against Cuomo led by Daniel Arbeeny, of Brooklyn, who alleged that the former governor’s nursing home policy caused his father’s death in 2020. On March 25 of that year, Cuomo signed a directive ordering nursing homes to take patients who tested positive for the COVID-19 respiratory illness. Cuomo also faced controversy over his administration’s undercounting of nursing home-related COVID-19 deaths. The decision concludes the most high-profile civil litigation against Andrew Cuomo over the nursing home scandal. The Supreme Court was the last resort Daniel Arbeeny had in his lawsuit against Andrew Cuomo.

**Portfolio Risk Narrative — May 2026 | Monthly Risk Committee Review**

May 2026 presents a meaningful deterioration across all three primary dispute metrics simultaneous with a sharp contraction in processing volume, a combination that demands committee attention. Total processing volume fell $406,966 month-over-month to $2.33M, a 14.9% decline from April's $2.74M and the lowest volume month in the trailing twelve. That volume compression alone would be unremarkable in isolation—seasonal softness and merchant mix shifts can explain short-term drawdowns—but the fact that chargeback, refund, and reversal rates all moved adversely in the same period indicates the decline is not clean. When volume drops and dispute rates rise simultaneously, it typically signals either a concentration effect where lower-risk, high-volume merchants pulled back disproportionately, or that a subset of the remaining book is generating elevated friction. Either interpretation warrants merchant-level decomposition before close of the review cycle.

The chargeback rate is the most operationally urgent signal this month. At 0.5525%, May represents an 18-basis-point spike from April's 0.4683% and sits as the second-highest weighted CB rate in the trailing twelve, exceeded only by August 2025's 0.5794%. The twelve-month trendline has not been directionally clean—CB rate has oscillated between a low of 0.4683% (April 2026) and that August 2025 peak—but the May reading breaks a three-month improving sequence that ran from February through April, which had brought the rate to its trailing-year low. That reversal of a favorable trend is more concerning than any single-month absolute level. The refund rate reinforces this read: at 5.0416%, it matches March 2026 as the highest refund rate in the dataset and represents a 36-basis-point deterioration from April. Elevated refund rates at this magnitude often serve as a leading indicator of chargeback pressure to come, as they reflect customer dissatisfaction being resolved at the merchant level before escalating to issuer disputes. The reversal rate also ticked up 4.75 basis points to 1.1158%, though this remains within the mid-range of the trailing twelve and is not independently alarming.

The committee should treat May as a yellow flag that has the potential to become a red flag by June if the volume recovery does not materialize or if the merchant concentration thesis is confirmed. The priority action is a segmented attribution run isolating which merchant categories or individual merchants account for the CB and refund rate spikes—given the volume compression, it is plausible that a small number of accounts are disproportionately driving the weighted averages. Additionally, if volume remains suppressed in June, the portfolio's absolute dispute counts may look manageable while the rates continue to signal structural stress, which risks masking real exposure in any card network monitoring calculations that use rate-based thresholds. Risk Management recommends flagging any merchant currently running a trailing-three-month CB rate above 0.80% for enhanced monitoring and considering whether the volume decline warrants a conversation with the commercial team about pipeline health in the segments that contracted.

json.title: Solstice Solar

reviews.name: Steven Morgen
reviews.text: Gage was very knowledgeable and helpful in explaining how the system works, how the installation process happens, what to expect, how much the installation will cost, and how to work with the system once it was installed. In other words, he was there for the whole process “from soup to nuts.” The solar panels and backup batteries are working perfectly, just as expected. Overall we are very happy with this system and the service we were provided.
reviews.responseFromOwnerText: Thank you so much for the review Steven.  We are so excited to hear that Gage was able to walk you through the process and set the proper expectations.  Welcome to the Solstice Solar family and should you need anything we know you have Gage, but you also have the entire Solstice team here to support you.

reviews.name: George Panaritis
reviews.text:
I’ve been researching solar and battery solutions extensively while preparing to move into a new home, and I can honestly say my experience with Gage and Solstice Solar has been exceptional from start to finish.

What stood out most was the level of transparency, patience, and education throughout the process. Gage never applied pressure or tried to “sell” me into a decision. Instead, he took the time to walk through multiple scenarios, including cash purchase options, prepaid PPA structures, long-term ownership implications, warranties, transfer considerations, and realistic expectations around costs and savings.

As someone who likes to fully understand the numbers and technology before making a major investment, I appreciated how responsive and informative he was during every conversation. He consistently answered detailed questions thoroughly and professionally, even when I needed time to think things through.

Whether I ultimately move forward immediately or later down the road, this has easily been one of the most professional and consultative experiences I’ve had while evaluating home energy solutions.

Highly recommend Gage and the Solstice Solar team if you value honesty, education, and a no-pressure approach.
reviews.responseFromOwnerText:
Thank you so much, George!

We strive to ensure every homeowner interested in exploring solar is treated with the same level of care and respect that you experienced. Gage truly sets the gold standard in that area, as he takes tremendous pride in what he does and never wants a homeowner to feel pressured or coerced into making a decision.

At Solstice, we’ve built a strong reputation around that philosophy because solar is a significant investment in a home and should never be taken lightly. Our goal is always to educate first, answer questions honestly, and allow homeowners to make the decision that feels right for them.

We truly appreciate the opportunity to work with you throughout this process and hope that, when YOU are ready, we’ll have the chance to officially welcome you to the Solstice family!

reviews.name: Hakimuddin Boxwala
reviews.text:
I was considering Solar roof and battery back for my home,  got in touch with Alfred Bongato to understand the different options.
Alfred is an expert and explained me the technical and financial aspects of the system he shared all the details with transparency.
I will recommend Alfred at Solistice if you are considering a solar system for your home
reviews.responseFromOwnerText:
Thank you so much for your kind words Hakimuddin, and for taking the time to share your experience! We’re thrilled to hear that Alfred was able to clearly explain both the technical and financial aspects of solar and battery storage while providing the transparency homeowners deserve when making such an important decision.

At Solstice, we believe education and honesty should always come first, and Alfred does an outstanding job representing those values every day.

We truly appreciate your recommendation and look forward to the opportunity to help you further whenever you’re ready to move forward with your solar journey!

reviews.name: Marty Simpson
reviews.text: We are beyond happy with our solar and battery storage system and our choice of suppliers/installers. The crew was great to a person and Gage Mueller-our consultant/guide/therapist thru the process-is in a league of his own. We did our level best to wear him out with questions and more questions and then a few more questions. After lots of independent research we had more questions. And long after lessor mortals would have run from us (and redirected us to their competitors) we realized that we should have just followed Gage’s guidance from the start, because it was clearly the best advice for our objectives and budget. Gage is a pleasure to work with and consistently went above and beyond to be clear with details, forthright and responsive. Truly couldn’t ask for a more professional or enjoyable experience.
reviews.responseFromOwnerText: Thank you so much Marty!  We are excited to welcome you to the Solstice Solar Family.  We are even more excited to hear that Gage and the crew went above and beyond to ensure you got the system you envisioned.  We do our absolute best to make sure our clients know that we are here for them, no matter the situation.  Should you need anything in the future, please don't hesitate to reach out to Gage or anyone else from the Solstice team as we are all here to assist in anyway that we can.  We are very happy to be part of your solar journey!

reviews.name: Catalina Leano
reviews.text: We had an amazing experience with Solstice Solar! A heartfelt thank you to Ashley for personally reaching out to troubleshoot our concerns. Sam came by and was incredibly helpful and knowledgeable, swiftly resolving our issue while enhancing our understanding of the solar panels and battery system. We can’t recommend Solstice Solar enough for their exceptional service and support! 🌞✨
reviews.responseFromOwnerText: Thank you so much Catalina!!!  We are so excited to have you as part of the Solstice Family and that Ashley and Sam were able to get you taken care of in a timely manner.  Please know that we are here to help in any way that we can moving forward, so please don't hesitate to reach out should you need any further assistance.

reviews.name: Husein Raja
reviews.text: Gage helped me navigate everything I needed to know about my solar roof that I got with a new home purchase; understanding how it works, which REP to go with, what I need to do for maintenance, expanding my system with backup batteries, etc. I highly recommend Solstice Solar for all your solar roof needs.
reviews.responseFromOwnerText: Thank you so much Husein!  Congratulations on the new home and we are so happy to hear about your experience with Gage and Solstice so far.  Should you need anything in the future we are here to help!

reviews.name: Ramona Moore
reviews.text: I now wish I knew more  about their three day policy to change ones mind. At this point I do not think having these panels was worth it, I was paying 125 a month for the panels and still paying a 280$ electric bill. Wasn't saving any money, you'll do the math .
reviews.responseFromOwnerText:
Thank you for reaching out.  We’re truly sorry to hear that your experience has not met your expectations. Going solar is a major investment, and we understand how frustrating it can feel when the savings don’t align with what you anticipated.

Every home’s energy usage, electricity plan, and system performance can vary significantly, and our goal is always to ensure homeowners fully understand both the benefits and limitations before moving forward. We also understand your concerns regarding the cancellation period and regret that you feel you didn’t have all the information needed at the time.

We would genuinely appreciate the opportunity to review your system, energy usage, and utility billing with you to better understand what’s happening and see if there may be solutions available to improve your overall experience.

Please feel free to reach out to us directly—we’d welcome the chance to help.

reviews.name: Burt Chrisman
reviews.text: Had Mr. Gage come out to check if the hail damaged my solar panels. While here he cleaned my panels, that was very nice.
reviews.responseFromOwnerText: Thank you so much for the review Burt!  We were glad to hear there was no hail damage and the panels were cleaned.

reviews.name: Vanessa Means
reviews.text: I wasn’t very familiar with solar systems before this, but the team explained everything in a simple and understandable way. They didn’t overwhelm me with technical terms. Installation was completed within two days, and the crew worked professionally. There was a minor issue with the monitoring app initially, but it was fixed quickly. Since then, I’ve been able to track my energy production without any problems. It’s been a few months, and I’m already seeing a noticeable reduction in electricity costs, which makes the investment feel worthwhile.
reviews.responseFromOwnerText: Welcome to the Solstice Family Vanessa!  We have tried our best to relay to all of our employees that explaining and understanding how a system will work is key to customer happiness.  We are so glad to hear that these objectives were met and that you were able to understand and are now seeing the benefits of what you solar system can provide for you.  Our relationship is just beginning, so please don't hesitate to reach out should you need any further assistance.  You are now part of the family and we want to ensure your system is working as expected.  Thank you so much for taking the time to write a review for us.

reviews.name: Bill Albee
reviews.text: Excellent service. They came out right away, diagnosed the issue with my panels and fixed it right away. I highly recommend their services.
reviews.responseFromOwnerText: Hi Bill!  Thank you so much for putting your faith in trust in our team to get you taken care of!  Should you need anything in the future please don't hesitate to give us a call.

reviews.name: Patrick Cruz
reviews.text: Great experience with Gage.  He was knowledgeable, patient, and never pushy. Instead of rushing me, he gave me multiple options and clearly explained each one. I felt confident making a decision without any pressure. I already have a solar panels running and thinking of purchasing a backup battery to do batery arbitrage to lower my bill.  but instead suggested to try free nights plan first before I make my decision.  Highly recommend!
reviews.responseFromOwnerText: Thank you so much Patrick!  We are excited to have built some trust with you around how we like to handle our clients and their needs.  Please keep us posted on how the free night plan works out for you and if the time comes when you are ready for a battery, Gage will be there to help you out.  Should you need any additional help or guidance we are all here to help however we can.

reviews.name: Mahmoud Alagha
reviews.text: I'd give Gage 10 starts, I was struggling to find the best backup system for my solar, and he explained in details every scenario, very knowledgeable and trustworthy person.
reviews.responseFromOwnerText: WOW Thank you so much Mahmoud.  We are so happy to hear Gage was able to help you understand the options that will be the best solution for your home.  We take great pride in ensuring our employees educate and inform not only our clients, but anyone interested in learning more!!!

reviews.name: Olia Palmer
reviews.text: Our inverter died and our solar-panel installation company had disappeared. Finding Solstice Solar was a relief and, as we worked with them to set our system back to working, we realized just how lucky we were to find them. Ashley was terrific at keeping us informed and Abdel was great at explaining things as he worked on our system over two days. We’re back online supplying energy to the grid. Thanks!
reviews.responseFromOwnerText: Thank you so much Olia!  We are very happy you have found us as well.  We know the solar world can be tricky to navigate, but just know you are now part of the Solstice Family and we are here to help with anything you need moving forward.  Ashley and Abdel along with the rest of our company take customer service extremely seriously as the customer experience is what it is all about!

reviews.name: Telma RODRIGUEZ
reviews.text: Mucha experiencia buenas, con esta compañía, la compañía que me instaló, cerró y hablé a Solstice Solar y ellos me pudieron ayudar con mi sistema y ahora está funcionando completamente y también me ayudaron a buscar otra compañía de luz
reviews.textTranslated: I had many good experiences with this company. The company that installed my system closed down, and I contacted Solstice Solar, who were able to help me with my system, and now it's fully operational. They also helped me find another electricity provider.
reviews.responseFromOwnerText:
Hi Telma! Thank you so much for your review. We’re very happy to hear that we were able to help you. We take great pride in making sure all solar homeowners know they have somewhere to turn if their original installer goes out of business. If you need any assistance in the future, please don’t hesitate to reach out. Welcome to the Solstice family!

Si necesitas cualquier ayuda en el futuro, no dudes en comunicarte con nosotros. ¡Bienvenida a la familia Solstice!

reviews.name: Jesse Flores
reviews.text: Solstice is in my opinion one of the greatest installers in the Houston area. Working with them over the years I’ve been fortunate enough to provide my clients the best service and quality when going solar. They’re always communicating with dealers as well as clients, getting installs completed in a timely manner.
reviews.responseFromOwnerText: Thank you Jesse!  We love our dealer network and want to ensure their success as we want to ensure ours.  Keep em coming as we are here to help!

## Kratom Spot Buyers Guide - FAQs

New to kratom or looking for more information? Our comprehensive guide covers all your questions, helping you make informed decisions about the best kratom for your needs.

What is kratom?
+-

Kratom, scientifically known as Mitragyna speciosa, is a tropical tree native to Southeast Asia, particularly in countries like Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia, and Papua New Guinea. The leaves of the kratom tree have been used for centuries by indigenous cultures for various purposes. When consumed, kratom leaves can produce a variety of effects that vary depending on the strain and dosage.

Kratom is commonly available in several forms, including powders, capsules, and teas. It is important to note that while kratom is widely used and available, it should be approached with caution and an understanding of its properties. As with any natural product, individual experiences with kratom can vary, and it’s recommended to start with small amounts to gauge its effects.

What are the strains and colors of Kratom?
+-

Kratom is categorized into different strains based on the region it is grown in and the color of the veins in the leaves. The most common strains are Green, Red, and White, each offering unique characteristics:

- Green Vein Kratom: Known for its balanced effects, green vein kratom is often described as being moderate in strength. It’s a popular choice for those looking for a balanced experience.

- Red Vein Kratom: Typically, red vein kratom is known for its calming properties. The red strains are often preferred by those seeking a more relaxing experience.

- White Vein Kratom: White vein kratom is usually associated with energizing effects. It’s often chosen by individuals who are looking for a more uplifting experience.


These strains can be further divided based on their region of origin, such as Borneo, Bali, and Thai kratom, which can also influence their effects. It’s essential to experiment with different strains to find the one that best suits your needs.

Is kratom legal?
+-

The legality of kratom varies significantly depending on the country and even within regions of a country. In the United States, for example, kratom is legal in most states but is banned in a few, including Alabama, Arkansas, Indiana, Rhode Island, Vermont, and Wisconsin. Some states have specific regulations or age restrictions, so it’s important to check local laws before purchasing or consuming kratom.

Internationally, the legality of kratom is just as varied. Some countries have completely banned kratom, while others allow its sale and consumption with certain regulations. Always stay informed about the legal status of kratom in your area or any place you plan to visit.

What are the best kratom strains for the first timers?
+-

For those new to kratom, starting with a strain that is balanced in its effects can be beneficial. Green vein strains, such as Green Malay or Green Maeng Da, are often recommended for beginners because they provide a moderate balance of energizing and calming effects. These strains offer a gentle introduction to kratom without being too overwhelming.

It’s also advisable to start with small amounts to gauge how your body responds to kratom. Everyone’s body chemistry is different, so what works well for one person may not have the same effect on another. Gradually exploring different strains and understanding their unique properties can help you find the one that best meets your preferences.

How old do I have to be to purchase kratom?
+-

In most places where kratom is legal, the minimum age to purchase kratom is typically 18 or 21 years old, depending on local regulations. Retailers often enforce these age restrictions to ensure compliance with local laws. It is crucial to verify the age requirements in your specific region before attempting to buy kratom.

Always purchase kratom from reputable sources that adhere to these regulations, as this not only ensures you are following the law but also that you are receiving a quality product.

Is kratom dangerous?
+-

Kratom, like any substance, carries potential risks, particularly if used improperly or in excessive amounts. While kratom has been traditionally used in Southeast Asia for its various properties, its safety profile is still under study. It’s important to approach kratom with caution, especially if you are new to it.

One of the primary concerns with kratom is its potential for dependency if used frequently or in large amounts. Additionally, kratom can interact with other substances, so it’s essential to avoid combining it with alcohol, prescription medications, or other drugs without consulting a healthcare professional.

To minimize risks, start with small amounts and gradually increase as needed. Pay close attention to how your body responds and avoid using kratom daily to reduce the risk of developing a tolerance or dependency.

How does kratom vary?
+-

Kratom varies primarily in terms of strain, vein color, and regional origin, each contributing to different effects. The three main vein colors—green, red, and white—indicate the general properties of the kratom, as discussed earlier.

- Strain Variations: Different strains, such as Maeng Da, Bali, or Borneo, offer varying effects due to differences in alkaloid profiles. For example, Maeng Da is known for its potency, while Bali is often chosen for its more soothing properties.

- Regional Differences: Kratom grown in different regions may have unique characteristics due to variations in soil, climate, and cultivation practices. For example, Thai kratom is often noted for its energizing properties, whereas Borneo strains might offer more calming effects.

- Preparation Methods: How kratom is processed—whether dried in sunlight, fermented, or ground into powder—can also impact its effects.


Understanding these variations is key to selecting the right kratom product for your needs.

Where is kratom found?
+-

Kratom is indigenous to Southeast Asia, where it grows naturally in tropical forests. The countries most commonly associated with kratom production are Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia, and Papua New Guinea. The climate and soil in these regions create the ideal conditions for kratom trees to thrive.

Kratom trees can grow up to 80 feet tall and produce large, glossy leaves. These leaves are harvested, dried, and processed into various forms, including powders, capsules, and teas, before being exported worldwide. Due to its popularity, kratom cultivation has become an important industry in these regions, with farmers employing traditional and sustainable methods to grow and harvest the plant.

What are the benefits of kratom?
+-

While many users report various benefits from using kratom, it is important to avoid making definitive health claims, as kratom is not approved by regulatory bodies for medical use. However, kratom has traditionally been used in Southeast Asia for its potential to produce a range of effects, which may include a sense of well-being, increased energy, or relaxation, depending on the strain and amount used.

It’s essential for consumers to do their own research and approach kratom with caution. The effects of kratom can vary widely based on individual factors such as body chemistry, tolerance, and the specific strain or product being used.

Do I need to consume kratom daily?
+-

Daily consumption of kratom is not recommended, especially for beginners. Using kratom every day can increase the risk of developing a tolerance, which may lead to consuming higher amounts over time to achieve the same effects. Additionally, regular use may increase the risk of dependency.

Many users find that using kratom intermittently, rather than daily, helps to maintain its effects without building tolerance. It’s advisable to take breaks between uses to allow your body to reset and to avoid any potential negative effects associated with frequent use.

What side effects does kratom have?
+-

Kratom can cause side effects, especially when taken in large amounts or if used frequently. Common side effects may include nausea, dry mouth, dizziness, and constipation. In some cases, users may experience more severe side effects such as agitation, sweating, or confusion.

It’s important to start with small amounts and gradually increase as needed to minimize the risk of side effects. Additionally, staying hydrated and avoiding the combination of kratom with other substances can help reduce the likelihood of experiencing adverse effects.

If you experience any negative reactions, it is recommended to stop using kratom and consult a healthcare professional.

What is kratom’s recommended dosage?
+-

There is no one-size-fits-all recommended dosage for kratom, as the appropriate amount can vary widely based on individual factors such as body weight, tolerance, and the specific strain being used. It’s generally advised to start with the smallest amount possible and gradually increase until the desired effects are achieved.

Users are encouraged to listen to their bodies and avoid taking more than necessary. Since kratom is not approved by regulatory bodies for medical use, there are no official dosage guidelines, and caution should be exercised to avoid overconsumption.

How often should kratom be consumed?
+-

The frequency of kratom use depends on individual preferences and goals. However, many experienced users recommend limiting kratom consumption to a few times a week rather than daily. This approach can help prevent the development of tolerance and reduce the risk of dependency.

As with any substance, moderation is key. Taking regular breaks from kratom use allows your body to reset and helps maintain the effectiveness of the product. Listening to your body and adjusting your usage as needed is crucial to having a positive experience with kratom.

![Woman with smartphone](https://www.upstart.com/static-tofu/_next/static/media/loanStepsHero.2c6124e2.webp?dpl=dpl_6raD6Vs4eRfJGmR9UVqqHkCQzqEb)

## Let us answer your questions

- chevron down

### What is a personal loan?









An unsecured personal loan is money borrowed from a lender that is not secured by property such as a house or car over a fixed period of time. While most loans through Upstart are unsecured, certain credit unions may place a lien on other accounts you hold with the same institution. There may be an option to secure your personal loan through Upstart with your vehicle, which will require a lien to be placed on the vehicle. It is important to review your promissory note for these details before accepting your loan.

- chevron down

### What is a car refinance loan?









A car refinance loan is a new car loan that usually replaces your current loan from a different lender. Refinancing your car loan can help you save money by lowering your APR or by reducing your monthly payments.

- chevron down

### What’s the difference between an interest rate and an APR?









The interest rate is only one factor of the cost of the loan. The total cost can be understood by the APR which is the annual cost of a loan inclusive both of interest rate and all other associated fees. For example, the cost of an origination fee is included in the APR. When comparing loan products, it is important to compare the APR of each product.

- chevron down

### How long will it take to get my money?









Personal loan funds typically are transferred on the next business day if the terms are accepted before 5pm ET Monday-Friday excluding holidays. If the terms are accepted after 5pm ET, on a weekend, or on a holiday, the funds will be transferred on the following business day.

- chevron down

### Will it affect my credit score?









Checking your rate on Upstart will not affect your credit score. If you proceed with your application after receiving a rate your credit score will be impacted. When you check your rate, we make a "soft credit inquiry." Soft credit inquiries on your report do not lower your credit score, but you may see when you view your report that this inquiry was made. If you are offered a loan and proceed with the application, a "hard credit inquiry" will be completed to verify the accuracy of your application. This action will be recorded as an inquiry on your report and it will impact your credit score.

- chevron down

### Do I pay a fee if I pay off my loan early?









There is no prepayment penalty for paying off a loan on Upstart early. You may pay off part or all of the loan at any time with no fee. By prepaying, you will pay less overall interest because the loan is outstanding for a shorter time.


## Is Upstart right for you?

\\* All unsecured personal loans through Upstart offer a fixed rate and range between 6.2% - 35.99% APR based on 5-year rates offered in March 2026. The lowest rates are only available to the most qualified applicants. Your APR will be determined based on your credit, income, and certain other information provided in your loan application. Not all applicants will be approved.

1. When you check your rate, we check your credit report. This [initial (soft) inquiry](https://upstarthelp.upstart.com/borrower-verification/soft-vs-hard-credit-inquiries-what-you-need-to-know) will not affect your credit score. If you accept your rate and proceed with your application, we do another [(hard) credit inquiry](https://upstarthelp.upstart.com/borrower-verification/soft-vs-hard-credit-inquiries-what-you-need-to-know) that will impact your credit score. If you take out a loan, repayment information may be reported to the credit bureaus.

2. As of publication in April 2026, and based on a comparison between the Upstart model and a hypothetical traditional model using Upstart data from Jan - Dec 2025. For more information on the methodology behind this study, please see Upstart’s Annual Access to Credit results [here](https://www.upstart.com/lenders/regulatory-compliance/access-to-credit-report/).

3\. ## Frequently Asked Questions

[View All FAQ's](https://henrymeds.com/faq)

What is Henry?

Henry is a telehealth service that makes it easy and affordable to get the medical care you need. We help people manage weight loss, perimenopause and testosterone hormone therapies, and erectile dysfunction, as well as other conditions.

It’s easy to get started—just answer a few questions about your health and lifestyle goals, and we’ll connect you with an expert provider. If medically approved, you’ll get your prescribed medication by mail within a week.

There’s no insurance required. Just a simple monthly bill with your provider visits, medication and supplies, and ongoing care included.

How does Henry work?

Henry makes it easy to get the personalized care you need in just a few steps.

Answer a few questions about your health and goals.
A licensed healthcare provider will review your information and recommend treatment if necessary.
If prescribed, you’ll get your medication by mail within a few days.

There’s no insurance stress or surprise bills. Just one monthly payment that includes your provider visit, medication and supplies, and ongoing care.

Who can use Henry?

Henry is open to all adults! To use Henry, you must:
Be 18 years or older.
Have a demonstrated medical need for treatment.
Live or have an address in one of the states we support.

How do I see a provider?

Click any “Get Started” button and answer a few questions about your health and lifestyle goals. You’ll then be able to schedule a provider visit face-to-face with a video call, or depending on your home state, choose an independent provider review without a video call. You and your provider will be able to exchange messages through our secure patient portal.

Does Henry require a long-term contract?

No long-term contracts! Henry offers convenient monthly plans, as well as longer term plans for certain treatments. You can easily cancel any time.

How soon will I receive my medication?

Most people receive their medication within 8-10 business days after they speak to their provider. Just a heads up, people in California may experience longer fulfillment times because of additional compound testing requirements.

What if I need to cancel?

You can cancel at any time in your account page of the patient portal, by contacting our support team at ask@henrymeds.com, or by calling 909-787-2342. If you’re on a multi-month plan, you may be required to pay out the rest of your balance unless you’re unable to continue for medical-related reasons as determined by a healthcare provider.

What is compounded medication?

Compounded medication is prescription medicine from a licensed provider that’s custom-made by a licensed pharmacist. Instead of a one-size-fits-all drug from big manufacturers, the pharmacist will mix or adjust ingredients in compounded medication to tailor to your specific needs. Because these medications are customized, they’re not FDA-approved in the same way as commercial drugs, but they do use FDA-approved ingredients.

Do I need insurance?

No, you don’t need insurance! Henry makes it easy to get the care you need without having to deal with insurance claims. Your provider visits, medication and supplies, shipping, and ongoing care are all included in your plan price—without any hidden or surprise fees.

\*If medically eligible

## About Defender

### Marine Outfitters Since 1938

Defender is an online store providing quality marine supplies, inflatable boats, and outboard motors. Our mission is to make boating more accessible with our vast catalog, fast shipping and expert service. Our knowledgeable, in-house staff is happy to answer your questions and help guide your purchase. That's how we continue to earn the trust of mariners worldwide, as we have since 1938.
We achieve this while providing excellent customer service through a knowledgeable and experienced staff. We keep a very large selection of products in stock which allows us to ship straight to your door with the least delay.
In addition to a vast selection of inflatable boats and outboard motors, we also offer a wide variety of boating accessories and gear to outfit your boat just the way you want it. From bilge pumps and life jackets to dock lines and electronics, we have everything you need to make the most out of your time on the water.
